can only give a maximum of 3 stars for Newthorpe Medical Centre because the standard of care has sadly declined to a worrying level. I had been a patient here for almost 19 years and used to consider it an excellent surgery, but in recent years the quality and consistency of care has dropped significantly.

First of all, I want to say I have nothing but praise for the nurses, healthcare assistants and most of the reception team. They have always been kind, professional and helpful. My issues lie specifically with aspects of GP care and communication.

The communication between the GP and hospital specialists has been extremely poor, to the point of being unsafe. My neurologist sent multiple letters over several months requesting that my epilepsy medication be added to my repeat prescriptions. Despite repeated phone calls from me and reassurance from the practice that it would be “sorted”, it never was. This left me repeatedly running out of essential epilepsy medication, relying on emergency 111 prescriptions, and at risk of seizures, ambulances and hospital admissions. Only after months of stress and pushing did the medication finally get added to repeats. This was not a minor admin error, it was a patient safety issue that could have had serious consequences.

Secondly, there has been a noticeable decline in empathy and willingness to properly investigate concerns. There is a tendency to dismiss symptoms as anxiety, weight related or “because of your age”, without considering family history, comorbidities or previous symptoms. Once a label like “psychosomatic” is placed in your notes, it feels like you are no longer treated as a credible patient. That kind of labelling not only undermines trust but actively prevents people from seeking help when they genuinely need it. I have found myself feeling embarrassed to call the GP, worried I won’t be taken seriously, even when dealing with measurable clinical issues.

Healthcare should feel safe and supportive. Instead, I have often felt dismissed, judged and unheard. I should not have to argue to be taken seriously, especially when my health history and objective readings justify concern.

This makes me genuinely sad to write, as this surgery has looked after me my entire life. But patients deserve to feel listened to, respected and cared for, not made to feel like an inconvenience. I genuinely hope Newthorpe reflects on feedback like this, because the community needs a surgery that patients can was a patient at this practice for years, and I feel it’s important to warn others about the level of unsafe clinical care I experienced.

After being discharged from ICU, the practice removed ALL of my asthma medications from repeat without any discussion: both my preventer inhaler and my reliever inhaler. This left me without essential medication for weeks. My symptoms escalated, and I ended up requiring antibiotics and steroids with no proper follow-up.

When I transferred to a new clinic, the pharmacist there immediately reinstated all my medication and expressed shock that a patient with a recent ICU stay had been left without a preventer or reliever inhaler. He described the situation as “dangerous,” which unfortunately matches my experience.

I tried repeatedly to explain my symptoms, but I felt dismissed every time. The modern asthma plan the clinic promotes was not applied to me at all. Instead, I was left unmonitored, unsupported, and at risk.
